newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bonds ended the week with a sparkle as market-positive U.S. employment data pushed 10-year OAT yields to their lowest levels in decades and shunted the March future to a contract high.
Analysts said the French debt market could edge up further but key U.S. inflation data at the end of next week could well limit the room for progress.

The March bond future set a new high at 131.38, equalling the future's historic high but eased back to end MATIF business at 131.28, buoyed with the U.S. by a bigger-then-expected U.S. unemployment rate arise and other labour market data.
"European markets were just waiting on the unemployment rise to advance," said FIMAT analyst Damien Jamet.
The yield fall on the benchmark 2006 OAT to 5.47, marked the first time in more than 30 years that yields slipped under 5.50 percent, he added.

Joanne Perez, analyst at Merrill Lynch, said domestic investors were nonethless carefully watching the spreads over Germany in the search for value and that there was still room for French debt to progress, but probably limited.
"It could continue to creep higher," she said.
The market was internationally driven today and there was still room for advances.
"I think the market will burn itself out but we need a couple of strong U.S. figures before doing that," she said.

The rise in January U.S. non-farm payrolls came in at quite a high 271,000 but the markets focused on a drop in working hours and a weaker-then-expected rise in earnings as favourable to steady interest rates in the United States.
The unemployment rate edged up to a higher-then-expected 5.4 percent. Key U.S. data due next week include January producer prices on February 13.
